claims.text: The initial material is untreated, cast, equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has limited oxygen resistance.
A thin aluminum oxide coating is to be applied to HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminum oxide coating will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Blocking oxygen diffusion will prevent oxidation of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminum oxide coating will improve the oxygen resistance of HfNbTaTiZr relative to the untreated alloy.
After high-temperature exposure, coated HfNbTaTiZr will undergo less degradation of mechanical properties than untreated HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will not significantly affect the alloy's mechanical performance.
The coated alloy is expected to retain a yield strength within 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
The coated alloy is expected to maintain its tensile ductility at 1000 °C.
The proposed oxidation exposure is 1000 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for 100 hours.
The degree of oxidation protection and mechanical-property retention may depend on coating thickness and uniformity.

contradictions.description: The boundary wording applies the 163–530 MPa range to both tensile ductility and yield strength, although MPa is a strength unit and cannot specify ductility.
